summary: Scope. Trial 2 of the continuous performance campaign. Trial 1 (perf-trial-20260906) merged: native CRC32, stored media + level-6 deflate in EPUBs, single-pass in-memory zip, streaming zip writer, lazy payload thunks, hash-while-streaming, keep-alive connection pooling, concurrent part/page/asset downloads, overlapped catalog fetches, latin1 byte loops for cfc1/descramble. This trial hunts the remaining headroom across CLI interface, decode loops, network orchestration, and RAM/storage.

Status. Baseline measured (below). Wave 1 lanes: (A) CLI startup — the import graph costs ~9 ms over the bare-node floor on every command; (B) cfc1 page-blob decode — the last hot CPU loop, looking for a word-at-a-time swap.

How numbers are produced. node --expose-gc perf/bench.mjs medians against a frozen copy of the campaign-start code in perf/baseline/; loop work uses the interleaved-median methodology in perf/loop-showdown.mjs.

waves.name: CLI startup — lazy command loading
waves.change: bin + index import every module (epub, openbook, read, …) before dispatching even `help`. Lazy per-command imports should cut most of the ~9 ms import-graph cost paid by every CLI invocation.

waves.name: cfc1 page-blob decode — word-at-a-time quad swap
waves.change: The adopted latin1+indexOf swap runs ~144 MB/s byte-by-byte. Trial: 4-byte DataView loads/stores to swap quads word-at-a-time, preserving the exact regex-compatible line-terminator semantics (alignment shift after \n \r \u2028 \u2029). Adoption bar: ≥15% with byte-identical outputs.
